newsitem.title: CANADA: FOCUS-Gulf Canada makes $720 million bid for Clyde.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Gulf Canada makes $720 million bid for Clyde.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd on Wednesday launched a 432 million British pound ($720 million) hostile bid for Britain's Clyde Petroleum, but analysts believe the Calgary, Alberta-based company will have to offer more to secure a deal.

Analysts said the rise in Clyde's shares, which surged 33 pence (54 cents) in London to close at 118 pence ($1.93), well above Gulf Canada's cash offer of 105 pence a share ($1.72), suggested investors were betting on the possibility of a trans-Atlantic bidding war.
"The share price is telling you -- and I tend to agree -- that this bid is not going to be enough," said Nick Antill, an analyst at the brokerage house BZW in London.
"This thing is not going to be a fait accomplis bid like has happened lately in Canada," said Martin Molyneaux, analyst with Calgary-based FirstEnergy Capital Corp.
Edinburgh-based Clyde quickly rejected the offer, saying it was "unsolicited and wholly unacceptable."
"This offer is far too low and anyway Clyde will continue to deliver better value to shareholders as an independent company," Clyde's Chairman Malcolm Gourlay told Reuters.
Gulf Canada's bid comes hot on the heels of the $1.23 billion acquisition earlier this month of London-based Santa Fe Exploration by Norway's Saga Petroleum ASA.

"The offer for Clyde follows Gulf Canada's previously stated desire to increase its activities outside its existing core areas of North America and Indonesia," said Gulf Canada Chief Executive J. P. Bryan, who has said for several months the company was hunting for an international deal.
Gulf Canada this year considered a bid for Australia's Command Petroleum Holdings N L which instead became the takeover target of Britain's Cairn Energy Plc.
Clyde's North Sea and Australian assets would provide Gulf Canada with additional core areas, and Clyde's Indonesian assets would complement its existing assets, he said.

Analysts who follow Gulf Canada said on Wednesday that Clyde's assets represented an attractive acquisition for the Canadian firm, which currently produces about 125,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day mostly in Canada and Indonesia.
Clyde produces about 39,200 barrels per day.
"It fits quite nicely," said Robert Hinckley, an analyst with Merrill Lynch in New York."

Hinckley pointed out that the purchase, which would initially be funded by debt to be paid down in 1997 with asset sales, the public offering of a stake in Gulf Canada's Asamera unit in Indonesia and a share offering, would pack more leverage onto Gulf's balance sheet.
However, Clyde's cash flow is two and a half times its planned capital spending, making the company cash-rich, he said.
Gulf Canada shares in Toronto closed down C25 cents to C$9.30. Its New York Stock Exchange-listed shares were unchanged at $6.875.
